RFC 7515 §4.1.4: "The "kid" (key ID) Header Parameter is a hint indicating which key was used to secure the JWS." When used with a JWK it is matched against the JWK's own kid. Keycloak OIDC layers page: look up and cache the public key from the certificate endpoint "with the Key ID (KID) embedded within the JWS".

JwtBearerOptions.RefreshOnIssuerKeyNotFound (aspnetcore-10.0): "Gets or sets if a metadata refresh should be attempted after a SecurityTokenSignatureKeyNotFoundException. This allows for automatic recovery in the event of a signature key rollover. This is enabled by default." ConfigurationManager.RequestRefresh Remarks: only if switch 'UpdateConfigAsBlocking' is set does it defer to the next GetConfigurationAsync, i.e. by default the update is not blocking. api resolves Microsoft.IdentityModel.Protocols 8.19.2 (obj/project.assets.json); docs page 8.19.1.

Round 2, new wording. Interval and default still verified: RefreshInterval is "the minimum time between retrievals ... or that a refresh was explicitly requested"; DefaultRefreshInterval: "5 minutes is the default time interval that must pass for RequestRefresh() to obtain a new configuration." But a RequestRefresh inside the interval does not obtain anything and is not queued; nothing 'waits'. The download happens when a later unknown-kid token calls RequestRefresh after the interval (the script's 5 s retries supply that).
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Requested downloads happen at most once per RefreshInterval (5 minutes by default), counted from the last accepted request. A request inside the interval is ignored; the first token with an unknown kid after the interval triggers the download. No api restart is needed.

claim_verdicts.evidence: JwtBearerOptions.AutomaticRefreshInterval: "Gets or sets how often an automatic metadata refresh should occur." RequestRefresh only re-fetches on first call or after RefreshInterval; between retrievals the configuration (keys) already retrieved is used. Keycloak OIDC layers recommends to "lookup and cache the public key". A key removed at Keycloak therefore still validates until the next retrieval.

Kubernetes docs, Distribute credentials securely: "If a container already consumes a Secret in an environment variable, a Secret update will not be seen by the container unless it is restarted." Round 2: §6 now says 'Only a container that starts again', matching this; claim text 'restarted or replaced' matches.

Deployments: "A Deployment's rollout is triggered if and only if the Deployment's Pod template (that is, `.spec.template`) is changed, for example if the labels or container images of the template are updated." Annotations under .spec.template.metadata are part of the Pod template.

Docker docs PostgreSQL guide: "When the container starts, it checks whether the PostgreSQL data directory is empty. If the directory already contains data, PostgreSQL starts immediately without running any initialization. If the directory is empty, the container runs `initdb` to create a new database cluster"; POSTGRES_PASSWORD "Sets the superuser password". No initialization with existing data means the variable does not change the role's password.

Follows from documented behaviour: the certificate endpoint "returns the public keys enabled by the realm" (Keycloak OIDC layers), and kid selects the verifying key (RFC 7515 §4.1.4). Once the old key is gone from Keycloak and the api re-downloads (restart = first retrieval), no published key matches the old kid, so unexpired old-key tokens fail signature validation.

Keycloak OIDC layers: certificate endpoint /realms/{realm-name}/protocol/openid-connect/certs "returns the public keys enabled by the realm, encoded as a JSON Web Key (JWK)". docker-compose.yml:43-47 web publishes "8180:8180". Line number is off: in rotate-signing-key.sh@stage-3 line 54 is '-s providerType=... -s parentId=...'; config.algorithm=["RS256"] is on line 55. Lesson text cites no line number, so only the ledger changes.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Keycloak publishes the realm's public keys at /realms/donhang/protocol/openid-connect/certs (the jwks_uri), reachable from the host at localhost:8180, each with kid and alg; the script gives its new key alg RS256 (line 55).
